parts.title: Part 2 — Note Completion
parts.script: Say naturally: Say naturally, as someone giving a short talk to a group of visitors: Good afternoon everyone, and welcome to the Termiz Regional History Museum. My name is Aziza, and I'll be your guide today. The museum was originally built in nineteen fifty-two, and it was fully renovated in twenty nineteen. We currently have twelve permanent exhibition halls. The most popular hall is the Silk Road hall, which attracts around forty thousand visitors every year. Please note that photography is allowed in most areas, but it is strictly forbidden in the manuscripts room, due to the sensitivity of the old documents. If you'd like a private guided tour, it costs twenty five thousand som per person, and must be booked at least two days in advance. The museum closes at six in the evening, but the gift shop stays open until seven.

parts.title: Part 6 — Note Completion
parts.script: Say naturally: Say naturally, as a lecturer speaking to students: Today I want to talk about the invention of instant noodles. The product was invented by Momofuku Ando, a Japanese businessman, in nineteen fifty-eight. Before that, Ando had actually experienced business failure several times, including the collapse of his previous company. He noticed long queues of people waiting outside ramen stalls after the war and wondered if noodles could be made faster and cheaper at home. His first successful product was called Chikin Ramen. To preserve the noodles, Ando used a method called flash frying, which removed moisture and allowed long-term storage. The product was initially considered a luxury item, since it was priced higher than fresh noodles at the time. Sales only increased significantly once the price dropped closer to that of regular noodles. Today, instant noodles are sold in over one hundred countries around the world.
